why_it_matters: The effective federal funds rate is the primary monetary policy target for the Federal Reserve. A steady 3.64% rate indicates no recent FOMC action to shift the policy rate and reflects stable conditions in overnight funding markets. Market participants tracking rate expectations use this data point to assess the current policy stance.
macro_context: The 3.64% effective federal funds rate represents the weighted average rate for overnight lending between banks. The stability at 3.64% across the five-day observation window (April 16-20) indicates no policy changes or market stress during this period. Actual FOMC target range details should be confirmed from official FOMC sources rather than assumed.
market_structure_context: The DFF series captures the weighted average rate for overnight transactions in the federal funds market. Stability at 3.64% from April 16–20 indicates orderly market functioning without pressure on overnight lending rates.
